items.title: Charles Calello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 21, 2025
items.q: So Frankie wanted me to join The Four Lovers. So I continued – I wanted to continue to go to school so I quit the band I was in and went to work with Frankie Valli and The Four Lovers playing bass.

ctx.x: What did he particularly notice? Because -- did you have horn players? How large was the band?

The band was five pieces. We had a trumpet player who played valve trombone and trumpet; and we had an alto player who played tenor; we had Fender bass, drums, and I played the accordion. So we also sang like the Four Freshmen and the Hi-Lo’s. Now I copied some of the arrangements off the record. The first one we started with was “It’s a Blue World,” which was relatively easy, especially ‘cause all the people in the band went to Arts High, they were all good musicians, they could read music, and as a result of it…
I have to write that comment down. “The triad band.” No sevenths allowed.
